rationale: The source bundles three obligations with different triggers and evidence. (1) follow-declared: when planning a journey's execution, default to the declared routes and train continuations without added scheduling or speculative transformations (statement, applicability, runtime boundary). (2) preserve-route-space: the plan must keep guards, error/exception routes, artifacts, terminal outcomes, side effects and ordering, not just the nominal path, proven by existing journey and acceptance tests (constraints term plus first half of evidence term). (3) baseline-before-speed-claim: fires only when someone claims a non-reference strategy is faster, and its only evidence is that baseline measurements were gathered first (second half of evidence term). The single rewrite failed on exactly this seam: folding the speed-claim duty into general evidence turned it into a citation requirement, and folding the constraints into why turned an obligation into a guarantee. Splitting gives each obligation its own trigger and evidence. Parts 1 and 2 were jointly mandatory in the source, so part 1 requires part 2. The original mandatory requires edge to planner.journey.execution-strategies is remapped directly onto all three parts, so every part carries the prerequisite on its own. The advisory/enforcement boundary notes are generic and go into a shared context node (id context.pattern-advisory-boundary).

parts.given: A plan follows a journey's declared routes and continuations.

parts.why: A nominal path is not the full route space. Following declared routes does not by itself guarantee these properties; the plan has to keep them.
